## My thinking this year

I'm fifty years old, been farming these seven mu for thirty years now. My wife and I are the only ones left on the land — our kid's working in town, sends some money back. So really it's just the two of us, and some days I'm running machinery for neighbors for extra cash, which means I can't be stuck in the field every day.

Same plan as always, more or less. Three mu of cotton on the west plot — that ground has been cotton for years, it's sandy and drains fast, cotton does better there than maize. Four mu of spring maize on the east side where the soil is heavier. I've thought about putting more land in cotton because the price has been okay, but picking cotton kills your back and we can't afford to hire much help. Four mu of maize is easier to manage — you plant it, you fertilize twice, you irrigate when it gets dry, you combine-harvest it.

**On the maize:** I'll plant in late April when the soil warms up, use a hybrid — Zhengdan 958 or whatever Old Wang at the agri-store is pushing this year, they're all pretty similar. About 4 kg of seed per mu. For fertilizer, I put down a compound fertilizer as base — maybe 40-50 kg of 15-15-15 per mu — then topdress with urea at the big bell stage, about 20 kg. That works out to around 18 kg of nitrogen per mu total. Extension guy last year said I could cut back to 15, but last time I cut fertilizer the ears didn't fill right, so I'd rather spend an extra thirty yuan and sleep at night. Irrigate once at jointing, once at tasseling if it doesn't rain. Spray for armyworm if I see them.

**On the cotton:** Plant mid-April under film. Cotton is fussier and more expensive to grow — seed alone is about 70 yuan/mu for good coated seed. Base fertilizer of compound around planting, then topdress at squaring and again at boll-setting. About 15 kg N total per mu. Cotton needs more phosphorus and potassium than maize so I use a 15-10-20 blend if I can get it. Pesticide is the big cost — aphids early, bollworm through the summer, have to spray four or five times. Pick by hand in September-October, me and the wife. If it's a good year we'll get a cousin down for a week to help.

**What worries me this year:** Diesel price is up, so tillage and irrigation both cost more. I'll irrigate the cotton twice instead of three times unless it's really dry. And I'm keeping some cash aside in case the well motor needs repair — it's been acting up.
